newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share prices hit 20-month high.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share prices hit 20-month high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices hit a 20-month high on Wednesday as rumours of healthy profits for the mainstay milling firms flooded the market, brokers said.

The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) all-share index rose 0.64 points to 236.35, its highest level since the beginning of March 1995. Turnover also rose to an average 21.35 million pounds ($6.28 million) from 14.16 million.
"It was a good day with lots of trade. The mills and the housing firms were tops," said Youssef Khalil of Delta Stockbrokers.

Central and West Delta Flour Mills was the day's most active stock but East Delta Flour Mills performed better. East Delta rose 2.25 to 38.75 in trade worth 1.56 million while Central and West Delta fell 1.51 to 58.49 in turnover of 25.6 million.

"There are very strong rumours that East Delta will make excellent profits not only for 1996/97 but for the next year as well. And Central and West is just stabilising, its still a very good stock," Khalil said.
Realestate firms Medinet Nasr Housing and Development and Heliopolis Housing and Development maintained their momentum, rising 5.00 pounds to 195 and 7.00 to 197 pounds respectively.

Rumours that Medinet Nasr would distribute a free share with a cash dividend fuelled the rise as did news that the firm sold a plot of land for 45 million at a tremendous profit. Heliopolis Housing rose on expectations the state would sell another equity tranche in the firm soon.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 346.11 from Tuesday's 345.57 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 168.74 from 168.18 points.
